content.value: A Schema defines a content type and the fields a Document of that type may carry — the contract that drives editing, rendering, and search.

In Barkpark a Schema names a content type (post, page, paper, task) and enumerates its fields with types drawn from Schema v2. Each field is either a scalar or a Reference Field pointing at another Document. Because every Document is
, the Schema is what gives an otherwise uniform primitive its shape inside the Content Model.
A Schema is read by every surface so they stay in lock-step:

items.value: renders the edit form from the field list — text inputs, reference pickers, PortableDoc block editors.
lays out columns and detail views from the same field metadata.
are derived from facetable fields, so what you can filter on in Search is a function of the Schema.

content.value: Because all three read one definition, adding a field in the Schema lights it up everywhere at once.
A Schema's Reference Field declarations are the blueprint the Edge Extractor follows when turning Documents into edges for the Content Graph. Whether a reference is scalar or
(a Schema v2 distinction) changes the Blast Radius of a change, so Schema authorship directly shapes graph topology.

Schemas are part of what the Capabilities Manifest exposes over the HTTP API v1, letting the bp CLI and other clients learn the content model without hardcoding it. For the full field-type catalogue, see Schema v2. Every mutation is validated against the Schema before it commits, so the same definition that drives the Surfaces also gates writes. A bare install's seed Schemas are exactly what makes the Fresh Install Invariant hold — core validates content with no plugin loaded.
